semanticCause: lspo_message JS concatenates the full string while C uses strlen and copies only the prefix before the first embedded NUL.
hypothesis: C-string sizing in level-message accumulation may differ from JS string concatenation for a valid message containing an embedded NUL.
supportedSetup: Production startup and mklev special loader, public des.level_init floor then public des.message calls. Input is an ordinary language string containing an embedded NUL (Lua escape \0, JavaScript escape \0). No arbitrary internal state mutation, special level, object/monster setup or player command.
expectedC: One alpha-NUL-omega message stores alpha. Appending tail stores alpha newline tail.
observedJS: One call retains alpha-NUL-omega; appending tail retains alpha-NUL-omega newline tail.
control: Ordinary alpha then tail and empty string then tail match C exactly, including newline insertion after an empty first message.
scope: Initialization buffer contents only. One cause, two targets. No rendering, screen, player-command, hidden-score or shipped-level impact claim. No connection to excluded coordinate-description work.
oracleProvenance: Exact upstream lspo_message body compiled with fixed single-string Lua-stack adapters. Each input byte string is hex-decoded with embedded bytes retained; luaL_checkstring returns its NUL-terminated storage pointer, and the unchanged C function chooses length using strlen. No new Lua runtime or full Lua parser is supplied. Public Lua fixture included to specify equivalent supported calls.

scannerOrigin.interpretation: Allocation edge prompted C string-sizing inspection; not a claim that JS needs manual allocation.
